solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Police officer in Cape, working with firm

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cape on maps
a machine that is working is on
firm and stable both mean steady and secure

explanation.surface: A police officer on a cape, teaming up with a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest rank of police officer in Britain, so the job title fits exactly.

clue.text: Person showing no emotion, caught getting on after nicking francs

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the word for getting on comes after the C and nicks, or takes in, the letter for francs

parts.note: someone getting on in years is oldish
F is the abbreviation for francs

explanation.surface: An unfeeling thief, caught in old age after pocketing some French money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after nicking' does double duty: the oldish piece follows C and takes in F.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold fish is an idiom for an aloof, unemotional person.

clue.text: Knight on silver horse

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A knight sitting on a silver-grey mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out steed.

clue.text: Cloth in river at Berwick

definitions.meaning: a rough woollen fabric from the Scottish Borders
the river that flows into the sea at Berwick-upon-..., on the England–Scotland border

explanation.surface: Fabric dropped in the water at a border town.
explanation.definitionFit: The woollen fabric was named after the Borders river, which reaches the sea at Berwick.

clue.text: Disturb canary, unfortunately, where it's protected?

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up out of order

explanation.surface: Don't upset the canary: sadly, it's in a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where it's protected?' refers back to the canary, a feathered creature kept safe in a reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve where wild birds are safeguarded is exactly where a bird such as a canary is protected.

clue.text: Single out hard school subject

indicators.note: out here means out of place, so the letters of single are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Singling out a tough lesson at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal, not part of 'single out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The national language is taught as a core lesson in British schools.

clue.text: Man behaving dishonourably — Conservative, notice

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A Tory politician caught behaving badly, as reported in a public notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is an old-fashioned word for a bounder who treats others, especially women, dishonourably.

clue.text: Victor perplexed coroner entertaining question on uniform

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece holds the other
a perplexed mind is muddled, so the letters of coroner are jumbled
in a down clue, on means placed above, so the question letter comes before the uniform letter

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzled coroner hosting an inquiry into someone in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perplexed' turns CORONER into CONEROR, and 'entertaining' sets QU inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who has won, a synonym for a victor.

clue.text: Dart in dartboard, a shocker

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the clue words dartboard, a shocker

explanation.surface: A dart lands in the board, a terrible throw.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'dartboard', the word 'a' and the start of 'shocker'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to rush or sprint suddenly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: You and I filling awfully large trousers?

indicators.note: one piece fills, or goes inside, the other
something done awfully is done badly, so the letters of large are mixed up

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: The two of us squeezed into a pair of enormous trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the letters to LEGAR. The question mark flags that trousers are just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are one example of clothing worn on the lower limbs.

clue.text: Information supplied by American group

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Data handed over by a US organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification group ranking above species.

clue.text: Joined female taken advantage of

parts.note: to be taken advantage of is to be used

explanation.surface: A woman who joined something only to be exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are fused have been melted together or united.

clue.text: Old friend causing impasse

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An old pal has brought matters to a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a deadlock where neither side can make progress.

clue.text: Backing students, a mistake

indicators.note: going backing means moving backwards, so the word for students is read in reverse

parts.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: Supporting the students turned out to be an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an informal word for an error or blunder.

clue.text: Derisive remark about prosperous gem dealer

indicators.note: about means around, so the derisive remark goes round the other piece

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking remark
well, as in well off, means prosperous

explanation.surface: A sneer aimed at a wealthy dealer in precious stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells jewels and precious stones is a gem dealer.

clue.text: Decoy, small, speaking with rough voice we hear

parts.note: talking is speaking

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word for a rough voice gives a word pronounced alike

parts.note: hoarse means having a rough, croaky voice

explanation.surface: A tiny decoy speaking in a croaky voice.
explanation.walkthrough: HOARSE and HORSE are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalking horse is a pretext or front used to hide real intentions, like a hunter's screen.

clue.text: Sauce boat raised

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A gravy boat lifted from the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as one thing, a gravy jug, but splits into the definition and a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is a tomato-based condiment.

clue.text: Get away at one in punt

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the word for punt

parts.note: a punt is British slang for a bet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Escaping at one o'clock in a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like the boat but is a bet; AT and I go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is an idiom ordering someone to leave, the same as get away as a command.

clue.text: Fling? Witness pair inside

indicators.note: the pair goes inside the word for witness

parts.note: to witness something is to see it

explanation.surface: An affair, as seen by a couple in the know.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of indulgence, and a fling is a brief wild time of enjoyment.

clue.text: Finally asks a male graduate for a dance

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word asks

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: At last a man with a degree asks someone to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom dance.

clue.text: First of mannequins wearing superb top

indicators.note: the first piece is worn by, so sits inside, the word for superb

parts.note: ace means excellent or superb

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word mannequins

explanation.surface: A model wearing a stunning top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like the garment but is the definition: a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point of something.

clue.text: Charlie spots accident

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Charlie notices a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like a verb, sees, but is a noun for skin blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a collision involving vehicles.

clue.text: Naval officer, mostly commendable, book omitted

indicators.note: omitted means left out, so the letter for book goes
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped from the word for commendable

parts.note: admirable means worthy of praise, commendable

explanation.surface: A sailor whose record is largely praiseworthy, apart from one missing book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ADMIRABLE to ADMIRABL; 'omitted' then takes out B.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest-ranking commander in a navy.

clue.text: Predictable way of life, in truth

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the clue word truth

explanation.surface: The truth is a routine existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a rut means living a dull, unchanging routine.

clue.text: Biblical character, drawn endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a drawn game is even, level

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture, sketched on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests sketching but means level, as in a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is the first woman in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: One holding the purse strings in power may, somehow, by changing rates

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters of may are rearranged
changing signals the letters of rates altered into a new order

explanation.surface: The treasurer in charge may alter interest rates.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: the word after 'may' rearranges it into AYM, and 'changing' turns RATES into ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who controls the purse strings decides spending, the role of the official who pays out wages.
